title: Apple Design System
description: Published React design system with a shadcn-style CLI: per-component versioning and rollback by git SHA
longDescription: A React 19 design system inspired by macOS, iOS and VisionOS, published to npm as @smart-coder-labs/apple-design-system. The interesting part is not the components — it is the distribution model: the CLI copies source into your project instead of importing a black box, detects your framework, strips 'use client' when the target is not RSC, and tracks each component's version and install history so any component can be rolled back to an exact published git SHA. This portfolio consumes it.

data.label: Component Source
data.description: The components/ tree — the single source of truth
data.details: React 19 components built on Radix UI primitives for accessibility and Framer Motion for the Apple-style motion language. Each component owns its folder, README and changelog; there is no compiled component bundle shipped to consumers.

data.label: registry.json
data.description: Generated manifest: versions, dependencies, git SHAs
data.details: Built by scripts/build-registry.ts. Records every component's current version, its inter-component dependencies and the exact git SHA of each published version. Recording the SHA is what makes rollback work without maintaining a tag per component.

data.label: CLI
data.details: Published as the `apple-design-system` bin. `init` detects the framework and writes design-system.json; `add` resolves inter-component dependencies transitively; `update` pulls the latest registry version; `rollback` checks out a prior version by its recorded SHA.

data.label: Framework Detector
data.description: Next.js · Vite · Astro · Remix / React Router
data.details: Decides the `rsc` flag. With rsc:true (Next.js App Router) components keep their 'use client' directive; with rsc:false (Vite, Astro, Remix, Pages Router) the directive is stripped on copy. This is the detail that makes one registry serve four framework families without per-framework forks.

data.label: design-system.json
data.details: Lives in the consuming repo. Records componentsDir, globalCss, the rsc flag, and for each installed component its version, status, install/update timestamps and full history array. It is the state that makes `update` and `rollback` deterministic.

data.label: Consumer Project
data.description: Owns the copied source — no black-box dependency
data.details: Components land as editable source under the configured componentsDir. This portfolio is one such consumer: @smart-coder-labs/apple-design-system sits in its devDependencies and src/styles/apple-ds.css carries the tokens.

keyFeatures.title: You own the code
keyFeatures.description: The CLI copies component source into your repository instead of importing a black-box package, so a component can be edited in place without forking anything.

keyFeatures.title: Rollback to an exact published version
keyFeatures.description: The registry records the git SHA of every published component version, so `rollback` restores precise historical source without maintaining a tag per component.

keyFeatures.title: One registry, four framework families
keyFeatures.description: Framework detection sets an `rsc` flag: Next.js App Router keeps `'use client'`, while Vite, Astro, Remix and Pages Router get it stripped on copy.

keyFeatures.title: Per-component version history
keyFeatures.description: `design-system.json` tracks each installed component's version, status and full install/update history, which is what makes update and rollback deterministic.
